findings: [P1] fm_adapter.py: validate_code accepts `return min(upper, max(value, lower))`, which passes every supplied vector but violates the requested expression when lower > upper. For value=5, lower=10, upper=0 it returns 0 instead of 10. Enforce the specified AST or add reversed-bound validation and explicitly define the supported numeric domain.

[P1] fm_adapter.py: FMAdapter.run ignores stderr on exit code 0 and accepts any schema-valid stdout. Consequently a provider failure or denial reported on stderr can still become a validated artifact and Review run. Define and enforce provider success/error diagnostics before accepting output; test valid JSON accompanied by failure stderr.

[P2] fm_adapter.py: Extraction grounding checks issue_id and status independently anywhere in the input. For `issue_id=bd-a status=closed; issue_id=bd-b status=open`, the incorrect pair bd-a/open passes. Validate that the pair belongs to the same source record, or reject ambiguous multi-record inputs.

[P2] recorder.py: Local runs enter Review without a commit, so their approval action hash binds only action, null commit, and issue_id. Distinct local results for the same Issue receive identical hashes, with no binding to task, input, or validated output. Bind local review requests to the run ID and validated artifact digest, and preserve that binding in recover().
requirements_checked: System model is fixed; PCC and other models are rejected with no fallback.
Reference input is passed as one argv operand after --; no shell evaluation occurs.
Generated code is compiled but never executed; the evaluator permits only bounded names and binary min/max calls.
Provider attempts are limited to two; execution has timeout, output limits, cancellation checks, and process-group cleanup.
Owner configuration gates local tasks; results are suggestions without automatic application.
Recorder captures inputs, outputs, validation failures, transitions, and Outbox events, subject to the findings above.
Reported tests and tiny synthetic benchmarks are supplied evidence, not independently executed verification or generalized quality evidence.
